content:
Apple is set to launch its first AI smart glasses as early as next year. The glasses will integrate Visual Intelligence and bring Siri into the real world. Here's what we expect.

Core Features

First and foremost, these are AI glasses, not AR glasses. That means they will primarily be operated via voice and camera, as they won't feature any display.

The lens will allow Siri to observe your real-world surroundings and answer questions, provide information, and translate signs. Another feature we expect to see on these glasses is the ability to ask Siri to save an image of something and remind you about it later—a feature we first spotted in a macOS 26.7 leak.

They will also have built-in speakers to play music and audio, so you can essentially use them as open-ear headphones.

On the other hand, however, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, these glasses may not be able to take photos and videos in the normal way. Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses have sparked major privacy controversies recently, so Apple may want to steer clear of that issue.

Design

Unlike Meta, Apple hasn't partnered with an existing eyewear manufacturer to design these glasses. According to Bloomberg, Apple has instead designed them in-house, with multiple styles currently in development:

A large rectangular frame reminiscent of the Ray-Ban Wayfarer; a slimmer rectangular design similar to the glasses worn by Apple CEO Tim Cook; larger oval or round frames; and a smaller, more refined oval or round style.

They are reportedly made from acetate, a material that is more durable and premium than plastic. Apple will also offer several colour options, including black, navy blue, and light brown.

Health Features

Apple is reportedly considering positioning this product as a health device in future iterations. This means they may include a heart rate monitor (similar to AirPods Pro 3), and could add additional software features (such as Apple Watch's Workout Buddy) to make them more practical.

Beyond that, it's unclear how Apple will make these glasses more useful from a health perspective—but don't expect to see that in the first-generation product.

Release Date

Recent reports indicate Apple will unveil the glasses at WWDC 2027, giving developers early access to prepare. The product will then ship later that same year, most likely in September, alongside the 20th-anniversary all-glass iPhone. You can learn more about that iPhone here.

Are you excited about Apple's first smart glasses? Let us know in the comments.
